payload.statement_nl: Let n be a positive integer and j an integer with 0 <= j <= n - 1. Assume F_n is differentiable on I_{n,j}. Then H_{n,j} is differentiable on (0,1), and for each real t in (0,1), H'_{n,j}(t) = F_n'(T_{n,j}(t)) / n.

result_payload.proof_nl: By the rescaling definition in this construction, T_{n,j}(t) is the affine map t ↦ (j+t)/n, and H_{n,j}(t) = F_n(T_{n,j}(t)). For t in (0,1) and 0 <= j <= n-1, we have j/n < (j+t)/n < (j+1)/n, so T_{n,j}(t) lies in I_{n,j}. Since F_n is differentiable on I_{n,j}, it is differentiable at each point T_{n,j}(t). Also, T_{n,j} is differentiable on (0,1) and T_{n,j}'(t) = 1/n. Therefore the chain rule applies, giving H_{n,j}'(t) = F_n'(T_{n,j}(t)) · T_{n,j}'(t) = F_n'(T_{n,j}(t))/n for every t in (0,1). Hence H_{n,j} is differentiable on (0,1), and the stated derivative formula holds.
result_payload.proof_summary: Use the standard rescaling definition H_{n,j}(t)=F_n((j+t)/n). The image of (0,1) lies inside I_{n,j}, so the chain rule gives H'_{n,j}(t)=F_n'(T_{n,j}(t))/n.

suspected_gaps: The lemma statement itself does not restate the definitions of H_{n,j} and T_{n,j}; the proof uses the standard rescaling interpretation implicit in the setup.
